title: Eviction Decision Auditor: simulation mode + rollback telemetry for continuous batching KV cache
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Continuous batching and GPU slab compaction interact with KV cache eviction decisions in ways that can produce correctness anomalies (stale KV reads, double-free of GPU slab memory, or missed cache hits under rapid in-flight request churn). We need a lightweight, deployable auditor that can run in a simulation mode against live traffic to validate eviction decisions, capture rollback-able traces, and provide deterministic telemetry for postmortem and automated policy tuning. This ticket designs and implements the auditor, its invariants, and a staged rollout plan that minimizes risk to production latency and memory safety.
acceptance_criteria: Auditor can run in simulation mode without changing live eviction outcomes
Auditor records deterministic decision traces for >= 99.9% of sampled eviction events with GPU slab identifiers and batch context
Telemetry format integrates with Console tracing hook and a new 'eviction-audit' dashboard
We can replay eviction traces in the staging replay harness and replicate at least one known stale-read bug
No measurable P95 token latency regression when auditor simulation sampling <= 5%
Automated regression alerts fire when auditor detects violation of core invariants (see invariants list)
design_decision_summary: We will instrument the eviction code path to emit an immutable audit record for each eviction decision. Records include: epoch, cache key prefix scope, slab id, lease token, batch id, caller origin (host/region), TTL calculation, and reason code (LRU/TTL/space-pressure/prefix-policy). Records are stored to an append-only ring buffer on the host and exported asynchronously to the observability pipeline. In simulation mode, the auditor computes what the eviction WOULD have done and records that alongside the actual action. Deterministic hashing of KV context ensures replays are deterministic. A bounded 'rollback' metadata field will capture corrective actions (e.g., immediate re-prefetch) when the runtime detects a violation within the same batch window. We avoid holding eviction locks for auditor operations to keep latency stable; instead we stamp decisions with monotonically increasing decision_sequence numbers and check them during later validation steps.
invariants: I1: Eviction decisions are monotonic per-slab: decision_sequence strictly increases for each slab to avoid races
I2: Lease safety: a KV entry with an active lease must not be evicted until lease expiry or explicit lease release
I3: Prefix affinity: eviction must not evict entries that are pinned by ongoing batched requests for the same prefix
I4: GPU slab ownership: memory free paths must only execute when slab decision_sequence is greater than the last allocator hold sequence
I5: Replay determinism: given the same decision_trace and batch inputs, the replay harness must produce the same eviction outcomes
proposed_steps: 1) Add decision_trace struct and ring buffer export in the runtime eviction path (simulation-only flag default off)
2) Implement deterministic context hasher (stable across builds) and attach to records
3) Wire asynchronous exporter to observability with compression and batching (max 1000 records/sec per host by default)
4) Implement lightweight validator that consumes traces and checks invariants, flagging violations to Sentry/Console
5) Build replay harness that accepts decision_trace artifacts and a captured request batch stream (staging only)
6) Add a rollback metadata flow: when validator sees an in-flight violation, emit a rollback suggestion in the trace and test in canary with no-auto-apply
7) Create dashboards, alerts, and run a 2-week sim-mode runway before any auto-correct rollout
migration_plan: Phase A (dev/staging): enable auditor simulation at 100% for staging hosts; exercise with fuzzed batch streams and known failure cases
Phase B (canary): enable simulation sampling 1% on production on a single region, monitor latency and ring buffer backpressure metrics
Phase C (ramp): increase production sampling to 5% over 3 days if cpu/backpressure healthy; enable invariant alerts
Phase D (action): after 2 weeks of stable sim-mode and no critical violations, enable richer traces and start automated post-facto analysis jobs
Phase E (auto-mitigate): gated behind signoff; do not auto-apply rollback actions until dedicated safety review and runbook exist
test_plan: Unit tests for decision_trace encoding/decoding and deterministic hasher
Microbench for ring buffer write path under sustained eviction churn (target < 1% CPU overhead at 5% sampling)
Integration: replay harness validates at least three historical incidents reproduced from incident-db
Chaos test: simultaneous continuous-batching flood + slab compaction in staging with auditor enabled
End-to-end: Console dashboard ingestion + alerting smoke test
rollout_plan: Start in staging with simulation flag on and export retained for 7 days
Canary 1% in us-west-2 for 48h, evaluate latency/backpressure
If green, ramp to 5% sampling across primary regions over 72h
Runbook: if P95 latency increases by >5% or ring buffer backlog > 90% for >5min, immediately disable auditor on that host group
Postmortem cadence: weekly review of violations for the first month
risks: Ring buffer growth causing host memory pressure under misconfiguration
Deterministic hasher drift between builds leading to non-reproducible replays
Telemetry overload increasing observability costs if sampling not throttled
False positives from validator causing noisy alerts and operator fatigue
